questions.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
questions.description:
### Problem

Read a single line containing lowercase letters (`a`-`z`) — the line may be **empty**. Find the **longest contiguous substring** that contains no repeated character, and print that substring.

If more than one substring ties for the longest length, print the one that **starts earliest** in the input.

### Input

One line of lowercase letters (`0` to `60` characters). The line may be empty.

### Output

The longest substring with no repeated characters. If the input line is empty, print nothing (the expected output is the empty string).

### Example

Input:
```
abcabcbb
```

Output:
```
abc
```

`abc` (length 3, starting at index 0) is the longest run with no repeats — later windows such as `bca`, `cab`, and `abc` (again) are also length 3 but start later, so the earliest one, `abc`, is printed.

### Another example (tie-break)

Input:
```
aabbcc
```

Output:
```
ab
```

Both `ab` (index 1-2) and `bc` (index 3-4) are length-2 windows with no repeats, and no longer window exists. Since they tie, the earliest one — `ab` — is printed.

testCases.description: normal case with a repeated character
all characters distinct - whole string is the answer
all characters identical - single character answer
tie between two equally long windows - earliest start wins
repeat is not adjacent to the earlier occurrence
empty line - expected output is empty
